issue.title: Move tool_adoption_report pairing, classification, and aggregation into the Rust core
issue.description:
`tools/tool_adoption_report` pairs each agent's normalized LLM tool-call records by `tool_use_id`, classifies heavy (>=20 s) `just check` / `just check-full` invocations as wrapped in `sase tool run` or raw, and aggregates count and wall-time shares with their denominators, counting (never guessing) unpaired, negative, over-six-hour, truncated, and ambiguous records.

That is exactly the kind of deterministic, reusable domain logic the [[rust_core_backend_boundary]] litmus test assigns to sase-core: a web app, a CLI, or a TUI adoption surface would all need these numbers to match. Epic sase-135's plan says Rust owns the reusable logic, but phase 6 shipped the pairing, classification, and aggregation in Python to keep the phase from becoming a cross-repo change.

Remediation: move pairing, classification, and aggregation into `../sase-core/crates/sase_core/`, expose them through `sase_core_py`, and reduce `tools/tool_adoption_report` to record collection plus presentation. Keep the report read-only and keep the "counted, not guessed" treatment of unpaired and ambiguous records, which is the property the epic's DoD-12 baseline depends on.

Proposed by phase bead sase-135.6 (epic sase-135) as a PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP note; filed by the sase-135 land agent on 2026-09-20.

task_type_fields.proposal: Relocate the adoption report's tool-call pairing, heavy-invocation classification, and share aggregation from tools/tool_adoption_report into ../sase-core/crates/sase_core, expose them through sase_core_py, and leave the Python script as record collection plus presentation.
task_type_fields.why_out_of_scope: Epic sase-135's plan assigns reusable domain logic to Rust, but phase 6 (agent-adoption) was scoped to docs, memory, and a read-only report; implementing it in sase-core would have turned that phase into a cross-repo change with its own wire, bindings, and release sequencing.

payload.entry: Draft Python side found (sase-1g4.2.1.land, 2026-10-05): the sase-1g4.2.1.5 parity commit 8c8c47f720 accidentally included two untracked files from its workspace, src/sase/core/tool_adoption.py (a thin require_rust_binding('tool_adoption_report') adapter) and src/sase/tool/adoption.py (a 511-line report CLI that collects records and renders them through that binding). Nothing imports either file, and no sase-core revision defines a tool_adoption_report binding (git log --all -S in sase-core finds none), so the files are dead code. The sase-1g4.2.1 landing plan proposes removing them from the tree. Whoever implements this bead can recover the draft with git show 8c8c47f720:<path> as a starting point for the Python half.
